column1: 1:1|The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin.|Preserves priestly origin and location without identifying Hilkiah with another figure.
1:2|The **LORD**’s word came to him in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.|Keeps exact regnal year and parentage.

1:3|It also came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, when Jerusalem went into exile in the fifth month.|Retains full chronological span and fifth month.
1:4|The **LORD**’s word came to me:|Keeps transition from third-person heading to first-person testimony.

1:5|“Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you;\nbefore you came out at birth, I set you apart.\nI appointed you a prophet to the nations.”|Preserves prenatal vocation and nations scope without expanding into general doctrine.
1:6|I said, “Ah, Lord **GOD**! I do not know how to speak. I am only a youth.”|Retains protest and youth without assigning exact age.
1:7|But the **LORD** said to me, “Do not say, ‘I am only a youth.’ Go to everyone I send you to, and speak everything I command you.|Preserves repeated objection answered by comprehensive commission.
1:8|Do not fear them, for I am with you to rescue you,” declares the **LORD**.|Keeps promised rescue amid opposition rather than absence of danger.
1:9|Then the **LORD** reached out his hand and touched my mouth. The **LORD** said to me, “Look, I have put my words in your mouth.|Preserves physical prophetic commissioning.

1:10|See, today I appoint you over nations and kingdoms,
to uproot and tear down,
to destroy and overthrow,
to build and plant.”|Retains all six programmatic verbs and unequal four/two grouping.
1:11|The **LORD**’s word came to me: “What do you see, Jeremiah?” I answered, “I see an almond branch.”|Keeps named addressee and concrete vision item.
1:12|The **LORD** said to me, “You have seen well, for I am watching over my word to carry it out.”|Preserves almond/watching connection with explanatory note rather than invented English pun.
1:13|The **LORD**’s word came to me a second time: “What do you see?” I answered, “I see a boiling pot, tilted away from the north.”|Keeps directional wording of pot opening.
1:14|Then the **LORD** said to me, “From the north disaster will be unleashed on everyone living in the land.|Preserves north origin and comprehensive threatened population.

1:15|Look, I am summoning all the clans of the northern kingdoms,” declares the **LORD**. “They will come, and each will set his throne at the entrance to Jerusalem’s gates, against all her surrounding walls and against all Judah’s cities.|Retains thrones at gates and all cities beyond capital.

1:16|I will pronounce my judgments against them for all their wickedness: they abandoned me, burned offerings to other gods, and bowed down to what their own hands made.|Keeps three charges and handmade objects.

1:17|But you, tie up your robe, stand up, and tell them everything I command you. Do not be shattered by fear of them, or I will shatter you before them.|Retains readiness idiom and disturbing divine threat with repeated shatter.

1:18|Look, today I make you a fortified city, an iron pillar and bronze walls against the whole land—against Judah’s kings, officials, priests and people of the land.|Preserves three defenses and four opposing constituencies.
1:19|They will fight you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you,” declares the **LORD**, “to rescue you.”|Repeats rescue promise while explicitly retaining conflict.
2:1|The **LORD**’s word came to me:|Keeps introduction formula.

2:2|“Go and proclaim within Jerusalem’s hearing: This is what the **LORD** says:
‘I remember the faithful love of your youth,
the love of your bridal days,
how you followed me through the wilderness,
through a land never sown.|Retains female city-marriage image and unsown land.

2:3|Israel was holy to the **LORD**,
the firstfruits of his harvest.
All who devoured him incurred guilt;
disaster came upon them,’ declares the **LORD**.”|Keeps sacred firstfruits and devouring consequences.
2:4|Hear the **LORD**’s word, house of Jacob,\nand all the clans of the house of Israel.|Preserves both ancestral names and clans.

2:5|This is what the **LORD** says:
“What wrong did your ancestors find in me
that they went so far from me,
followed emptiness and became empty themselves?|Keeps accusation as question and hevel word-root repetition.

2:6|They did not ask, ‘Where is the **LORD**,
who brought us up from Egypt,
who led us through the wilderness,
a land of deserts and pits,
a land of drought and deep darkness,
a land no one crossed and no one inhabited?’|Retains cumulative wilderness hazards and absence of inquiry.

2:7|I brought you into a fruitful land
to eat its fruit and goodness.
But you came and defiled my land;
you made my inheritance offensive.|Keeps gift then defilement and divine ownership.

2:8|The priests did not ask, ‘Where is the **LORD**?’
Those who handle instruction did not know me.
The shepherds rebelled against me;
the prophets prophesied by Baal
and followed things that cannot help.|Retains all leadership groups and named Baal.
2:9|So I will still bring a case against you,” declares the **LORD**,\n“and against your children’s children.|Preserves continuing legal contention and generations.
2:10|Cross to Kittim’s coastlands and look;\nsend to Kedar and examine carefully.\nSee whether anything like this has happened:|Keeps west/east named comparison without replacing geography.

2:11|Has a nation exchanged its gods,
even though they are not gods?
Yet my people have exchanged their Glory
for what cannot help.|Preserves ironic contrast and Glory as divine reference.
2:12|Be appalled at this, heavens!\nShudder; be utterly desolate!” declares the **LORD**.|Keeps cosmic audience and three commands.

2:13|“For my people have done two evils:
they abandoned me, the spring of living water,
and dug themselves cisterns,
cracked cisterns that cannot hold water.|Preserves fresh flowing water versus failed storage metaphor.
2:14|Is Israel a slave,\na slave born in the household?\nWhy then has he become plunder?|Keeps actual enslaved status analogy.

2:15|Young lions roared against him;
they raised their voices
and made his land a waste.
His cities are burned, without inhabitants.|Follows read plural burned and retains lion imagery.
2:16|Even the people of Memphis and Tahpanhes\nhave grazed the crown of your head.|Preserves difficult grazing/shaving image and read city name.
2:17|Have you not brought this on yourself\nby abandoning the **LORD** your God\nwhile he led you along the way?|Keeps accusation and simultaneous guidance.

2:18|Now why take the road to Egypt
to drink Shihor’s waters?
Why take the road to Assyria
to drink the River’s waters?|Retains water metaphor for foreign reliance and named waterways.

2:19|Your own wickedness will discipline you;
your turning away will rebuke you.
Know and see how evil and bitter it is
to abandon the **LORD** your God
and have no fear of me,”
declares the Lord **GOD** of hosts.|Keeps self-punishing conduct and full divine title.

2:20|“Long ago I broke your yoke
and tore apart your bonds.
But you said, ‘I will not serve!’
On every high hill and under every green tree
you sprawled as a prostitute.|Retains written not-serve and pinned first-person broke; contrasting read transgress noted.

2:21|I planted you as a choice vine,
entirely sound stock.
How did you turn into
a degenerate foreign vine before me?|Preserves cultivated-vine identity reversal.

2:22|Though you wash with soda
and use soap in abundance,
the stain of your guilt remains before me,”
declares the Lord **GOD**.|Keeps material cleansing agents and indelible guilt.

2:24|wild donkey accustomed to the wilderness,
sniffing the wind in her desire!
Who can turn her back in heat?
None who seek her need weary themselves;
in her month they will find her.|Follows read feminine desire and retains sexual animal metaphor.

2:25|Keep your feet from going bare
and your throat from thirst.
But you said, ‘It is hopeless! No!
I love strangers, and I will follow them.’|Keeps failed warning and emphatic refusal.
2:26|As a thief is ashamed when caught,\nso the house of Israel is ashamed—\nthey, their kings, officials, priests and prophets.|Retains full group enumeration and caught-thief simile.

2:27|They say to wood, ‘You are my father,’
and to stone, ‘You gave birth to us.’
They turn their backs to me, not their faces,
but in trouble they say, ‘Rise and save us!’|Follows read us and preserves male wood/female stone parentage.
2:28|Where are the gods you made for yourself?\nLet them rise, if they can save you in trouble!\nFor your gods are as numerous as your cities, Judah.|Keeps challenge and city-god comparison.
2:29|Why bring a case against me?\nAll of you have rebelled against me,” declares the **LORD**.|Preserves reversal of courtroom accusation.

2:30|“I struck your children for nothing;
they accepted no discipline.
Your sword devoured your prophets
like a destructive lion.|Keeps divine striking and community violence against prophets distinct.

2:31|You of this generation, consider the **LORD**’s word!
Have I been a wilderness to Israel,
a land of thick darkness?
Why do my people say, ‘We roam freely;
we will come to you no more’?|Preserves rhetorical wilderness reversal and uncertain roam-free verb.

2:32|Does a young woman forget her jewelry,
a bride her wedding sash?
Yet my people have forgotten me
for days beyond counting.|Keeps bridal possessions and uncountable neglect.
2:33|How well you arrange your way to seek love!\nYou have even taught wicked women your ways.|Follows read feminine taught and preserves ironic skill.

2:34|Even on your skirts is found
the lifeblood of the innocent poor.
You did not find them breaking in.
Yet despite all this,|Reads the archaic second-person feminine found (XML HVqp2fs), preserving the absence of a break-in defense for killing the poor.

2:35|you say, ‘I am innocent;
surely his anger has turned away from me.’
Look, I am bringing you to judgment
for saying, ‘I have not sinned.’|Keeps false innocence and reason for judgment.

2:36|Why do you rush about so much,
changing your way?
Egypt will put you to shame
just as Assyria did.|Preserves foreign alliance switching and paired nations.

2:37|You will leave there too
with your hands on your head,
for the **LORD** has rejected those you trust;
you will not prosper through them.”|Keeps mourning/captivity gesture and failed trusts.

3:1|“If a man sends his wife away
and she leaves him and becomes another man’s wife,
will he return to her again?
Would that land not be thoroughly defiled?
Yet you have prostituted yourself with many lovers—
and would you return to me?” declares the **LORD**.|Keeps legal analogy and question reading of return; imperative possibility noted.

3:2|“Lift your eyes to the bare heights and look:
where have you not been lain with?
Beside the roads you sat waiting for them,
like a desert Arab.
You defiled the land
with your prostitution and wickedness.|Follows read euphemistic lie-with while retaining sexual force and ancient comparison.

3:3|So showers were withheld,
and the spring rain did not come.
Yet you had a prostitute’s forehead;
you refused to be ashamed.|Keeps drought consequence and forehead image.
3:4|Have you not just called to me,\n‘My Father, you are the companion of my youth!|Follows read you-called and retains overlapping family/companion imagery.

3:5|Will he hold a grudge forever,
will he keep it always?’
Look, this is what you say,
but you do every evil you can.”|Follows read you-say and contrasts speech with conduct.

3:6|In the days of King Josiah, the **LORD** said to me, “Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She went up every high mountain and under every green tree and prostituted herself there.|Preserves historical setting and female corporate personification.
3:7|I thought, ‘After she has done all this, she will return to me.’ But she did not return, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it.|Keeps frustrated divine expectation and sister witness.

3:8|I saw that, although I sent faithless Israel away and gave her a divorce document because of all her adultery, her treacherous sister Judah did not fear. She too went and prostituted herself.|Retains pinned I-saw opening and explicit divorce metaphor.
3:9|Treating her prostitution lightly, she defiled the land and committed adultery with stone and wood.|Preserves literal objects as metaphorical partners.

3:10|Despite all this, her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but only in pretense,” declares the **LORD**.|Keeps halfhearted return contrasted with actual repentance.
3:11|The **LORD** said to me, “Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.|Preserves comparative righteousness rather than absolute innocence.

3:12|Go and proclaim these words toward the north:
‘Return, faithless Israel,’ declares the **LORD**.
‘I will not look on you in anger,
for I am faithful in love,’ declares the **LORD**.
‘I will not hold a grudge forever.|Keeps northward address and return-turning word family.

3:13|Only acknowledge your guilt:
you rebelled against the **LORD** your God,
scattered your favors among strangers under every green tree,
and did not listen to my voice,’ declares the **LORD**.|Preserves confession requirement and metaphorical scattered ways.

3:14|‘Return, children who have turned away,’ declares the **LORD**,
‘for I am your husband.
I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan,
and bring you to Zion.|Retains husband/master ambiguity and exact gathering numbers.
3:15|I will give you shepherds after my own heart,\nand they will shepherd you with knowledge and understanding.|Keeps shepherd repetition for leaders’ task.

3:16|When you multiply and become fruitful in the land in those days,’ declares the **LORD**, ‘people will no longer say, “The ark of the **LORD**’s covenant.” It will not come to mind; they will not remember it or miss it, and it will not be made again.|Preserves striking disappearance of ark’s role and all negations.

3:17|At that time they will call Jerusalem the **LORD**’s Throne. All nations will gather there, to Jerusalem, for the **LORD**’s name. They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.|Keeps replacement throne image and nations gathering.

3:18|In those days the house of Judah will join the house of Israel. Together they will come from the northern land to the land I gave your ancestors as an inheritance.|Preserves two houses’ reunion and return direction.

3:19|I thought, “How I would place you among my sons
and give you a desirable land,
the most beautiful inheritance among the nations!”
I thought you would call me “My Father”
and would not turn away from following me.|Follows read feminine singular address and retains sons inheritance language.
3:20|But as a wife betrays her companion,\nso you have betrayed me, house of Israel,’\ndeclares the **LORD**.”|Keeps companion term and explicit national addressee.

3:21|A sound is heard on the bare heights,
the weeping pleas of Israel’s children,
for they have twisted their way
and forgotten the **LORD** their God.|Retains former cultic heights as lament location.

3:22|“Return, children who have turned away;
I will heal your turning away.”
“Here we are! We come to you,
for you are the **LORD** our God.|Marks change from summons to communal response and repeated turning.

3:23|Surely the hills are a deception,
the uproar on the mountains.
Surely in the **LORD** our God
is Israel’s salvation.|Retains compressed hill-uproar clause and doubled surely.

3:24|From our youth, Shame has devoured
what our ancestors worked for:
their flocks and cattle,
their sons and daughters.|Preserves personified Shame and sacrificed human children.

3:25|Let us lie down in our shame;
let humiliation cover us.
We have sinned against the **LORD** our God,
we and our ancestors,
from our youth to this day.
We have not listened to the **LORD** our God.”|Keeps collective confession’s generations and duration.

4:1|“If you return, Israel,” declares the **LORD**,
“return to me.
If you remove your offensive things from my sight
and cease wandering,|Keeps conditional return and relational destination.

4:2|and swear, ‘As the **LORD** lives,’
in truth, justice and righteousness,
then nations will bless themselves by him
and boast in him.”|Preserves oath’s ethical conditions and nations’ response.
4:3|For this is what the **LORD** says to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem:\n“Break up your unplowed ground;\ndo not sow among thorns.|Keeps agricultural preparation metaphor and specific audience.

4:4|Circumcise yourselves to the **LORD**;
remove the foreskins of your hearts,
men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem,
or my fury will burst out like fire
and burn with no one to quench it,
because of your evil deeds.”|Preserves embodied circumcision metaphor and unquenched threat.

4:5|Announce in Judah, proclaim in Jerusalem:
“Blow the ram’s horn through the land!”
Cry out at full voice:
“Gather! Let us enter the fortified cities!”|Keeps public alarm and collective refuge call.

4:6|Raise a banner toward Zion!
Seek safety; do not delay!
For I am bringing disaster from the north,
great destruction.|Preserves direction, urgency and divine agency.
4:8|So put on sackcloth, mourn and howl,\nfor the **LORD**’s burning anger\nhas not turned away from us.|Preserves speaker’s inclusion in threatened us.

4:9|“On that day,” declares the **LORD**,
“the king and officials will lose heart;
priests will be appalled,
and prophets stunned.”|Keeps all four leadership groups.

4:10|Then I said, “Ah, Lord **GOD**! You have surely deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You will have peace,’ while the sword reaches our very lives!”|Retains prophet’s accusation of divine deception without explaining it away.

4:11|At that time this people and Jerusalem will be told,
“A scorching wind from the wilderness’s bare heights
comes toward the daughter of my people,
not to winnow, not to clean—|Keeps destructive wind distinguished from useful farming wind.
4:12|a wind too strong for that comes at my command.\nNow I too will pronounce judgments against them.”|Preserves divine control and legal pronouncement.

4:13|Look, he rises like clouds,
his chariots like a whirlwind,
his horses swifter than eagles.
“Woe to us! We are ruined!”|Keeps approaching enemy and quoted communal cry distinct.
4:14|Wash the evil from your heart, Jerusalem,\nso you may be saved.\nHow long will your harmful thoughts lodge within you?|Retains cleansing and lodging imagery.
4:15|A voice announces news from Dan,\nproclaims disaster from Ephraim’s hills.|Keeps approaching warning’s named geography.

4:16|“Notify the nations!
Look, proclaim against Jerusalem:
besiegers are coming from a distant land;
they raise their voices against Judah’s cities.|Preserves watchers as siege force in context and foreign distance.
4:17|Like guards around a field, they surround her,\nbecause she has rebelled against me,” declares the **LORD**.|Keeps agricultural guard simile and feminine city.
4:18|“Your way and your deeds have brought this upon you.\nThis is your bitter disaster;\nit reaches your very heart.”|Preserves evil/disaster consequence and heart penetration.

4:19|My insides, my insides! I writhe!
The walls of my heart! My heart pounds within me.
I cannot keep silent,
for you have heard, my soul,
the ram’s horn and the battle cry.|Follows read you-heard address to soul and preserves bodily fragments.

4:20|Destruction upon destruction is announced;
the whole land is devastated.
Suddenly my tents are destroyed,
my curtains in a moment.|Keeps repeated destruction and personal dwelling imagery.
4:21|How long must I see the banner\nand hear the ram’s horn?|Retains prolonged sensory alarm.

4:22|“My people are foolish; they do not know me.
They are senseless children without understanding.
They are wise at doing evil,
but do not know how to do good.”|Keeps ironic wisdom and divine my-people voice.
4:23|I looked at the earth: it was unformed and empty;\nat the heavens: their light was gone.|Preserves Genesis creation-reversal vocabulary.
4:24|I looked at the mountains: they were quaking;\nall the hills were shaking.|Repeats I-looked frame and two landforms.
4:25|I looked: there was no human being;\nall the birds of the heavens had fled.|Keeps absence of humans and birds.
4:26|I looked: the fruitful land was wilderness;\nall its cities lay demolished\nbefore the **LORD**, before his burning anger.|Preserves fourth I-looked and repeated before.
4:27|For this is what the **LORD** says:\n“The whole land will become desolate,\nbut I will not make a complete end.|Keeps limiting assurance within total devastation language.

4:28|For this the earth will mourn
and the heavens above grow dark.
I have spoken; I have resolved it.
I have not relented and will not turn back.”|Preserves earth mourning and irreversible declared purpose.

4:29|At the sound of horsemen and archers,
every city flees.
They enter thickets and climb among rocks.
Every city is abandoned;
not a person lives in them.|Retains multiple refuges and city-person metonymy.

4:30|And you, devastated one, what are you doing?
Though you dress in scarlet and adorn yourself with gold,
though you widen your eyes with dark paint,
you make yourself beautiful for nothing.
Your lovers despise you; they seek your life.|Keeps cosmetics and lethal reversal of lovers.

4:31|I hear a voice like a woman in labor,
distress like one bearing her first child—
the voice of Daughter Zion, gasping,
spreading out her hands:
“Woe to me! My life is failing before killers!”|Preserves first childbirth and explicit attackers.

5:1|“Roam Jerusalem’s streets; look and find out!
Search her squares.
If you find one person who does justice
and seeks faithfulness,
I will forgive her.|Keeps single righteous person condition and female city pardon.
5:2|Even when they say, ‘As the **LORD** lives,’\nthey swear falsely.”|Preserves misuse of correct oath formula.

5:3|**LORD**, do your eyes not look for faithfulness?
You struck them, but they felt no pain;
you consumed them, but they refused discipline.
They made their faces harder than rock
and refused to return.|Keeps physical resistance and repeated refusal.

5:4|I thought, “These are only the poor;\nthey act foolishly because they do not know\nthe **LORD**’s way, their God’s judgment.|Marks observer’s hypothesis rather than narrator-endorsed generalization about poverty.

5:5|Let me go to the great and speak with them,
for they know the **LORD**’s way, their God’s judgment.”
But together they too had broken the yoke
and torn apart the bonds.|Keeps elite failure overturning initial hypothesis.

5:6|So a lion from the forest will strike them,
a wolf from the deserts will devastate them,
and a leopard will watch their cities.
Everyone leaving them will be torn apart,
for their rebellions are many
and their turning away is great.|Retains three predators and violent consequence.

5:7|“How can I forgive you?
Your children abandoned me
and swore by what are not gods.
I fed them fully, but they committed adultery
and crowded into a prostitute’s house.|Keeps divine provision and unfaithful response.
5:8|They were well-fed, lustful stallions,\neach neighing after his neighbor’s wife.|Preserves animal sexual metaphor and specific wives.
5:9|Should I not call them to account for this?” declares the **LORD**.\n“Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?|Establishes repeated judicial question refrain.

5:10|Climb through her vine rows and destroy,
but do not make a complete end.
Strip off her shoots,
for they do not belong to the **LORD**.|Chooses vineyard reading from shoots context; wall alternative noted.
5:11|For the house of Israel and the house of Judah\nhave thoroughly betrayed me,” declares the **LORD**.|Preserves both houses and emphatic betrayal.
5:12|They have denied the **LORD**, saying,\n“It is not he! Disaster will not come upon us;\nwe will see neither sword nor famine.|Keeps ambiguous denial wording rather than categorical atheism.
5:13|The prophets will become wind;\nthe word is not in them.\nLet this happen to them!”|Retains hostile assessment of prophets and retaliatory wish.

5:14|So this is what the **LORD**, God of hosts, says:
“Because you have said this,
look, I am making my words in your mouth fire
and this people wood.
The fire will consume them.|Keeps plural accusers to singular prophet shift and word-fire image.

5:15|Look, I am bringing a nation from far away against you,
house of Israel,” declares the **LORD**.
“It is an enduring nation, an ancient nation,
a nation whose language you do not know,
whose speech you cannot understand.|Preserves repeated nation and incomprehensible language.
5:16|Its quiver is an open grave;\nall its men are warriors.|Retains deadly quiver metaphor.

5:17|It will devour your harvest and your bread,
devour your sons and daughters,
devour your flocks and cattle,
devour your vines and fig trees.
With the sword it will shatter
the fortified cities you trust.|Preserves repeated devour and children as objects rather than harmonizing syntax to food-only loss.
5:18|Yet even in those days,” declares the **LORD**, “I will not make a complete end of you.|Keeps repeated limitation on destruction.

5:19|“When you ask, ‘Why has the **LORD** our God done all this to us?’ tell them, ‘As you abandoned me and served foreign gods in your own land, so you will serve foreigners in a land not your own.’|Preserves service-for-service reversal and land contrast.
5:20|“Announce this in the house of Jacob;\nproclaim it in Judah:|Keeps named audience and herald formula.
5:21|‘Hear this, foolish people without sense,\nwho have eyes but do not see,\nears but do not hear.|Retains paired unused faculties.

5:22|Do you not fear me?’ declares the **LORD**.
‘Will you not tremble before me,
who set sand as the sea’s boundary,
an everlasting limit it cannot cross?
Its waves surge, but cannot prevail;
they roar, but cannot cross it.|Keeps repeated cannot-cross and humble sand boundary.
5:23|But this people has a stubborn, rebellious heart;\nthey turned aside and went away.|Contrasts human rebellion with bounded sea.

5:24|They do not say in their hearts,
“Let us fear the **LORD** our God,
who gives rain in its season, autumn and spring rain,
and keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest.”|Preserves seasonal rains and harvest weeks.
5:25|Your offenses have turned these away;\nyour sins have kept good things from you.|Keeps consequences linked to preceding agricultural gifts.
5:26|For wicked people are found among my people.\nThey lie in wait like crouching birdcatchers;\nthey set a trap and catch human beings.|Preserves difficult hunter simile and human prey.
5:27|Like a cage full of birds,\ntheir houses are full of deceit.\nThat is how they became great and rich.|Keeps wealth attributed to trapping/deception.

5:28|They have grown fat and sleek;
their evil knows no bounds.
They do not judge the orphan’s case to secure justice,
and they do not defend the poor person’s rights.|Retains bodily prosperity and two denied legal protections.
5:29|Should I not call them to account for this?’ declares the **LORD**.\n‘Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?’|Repeats 5:9 refrain exactly in substance.
5:30|“An appalling, horrible thing has happened in the land:|Keeps double horror introduction.

5:31|prophets prophesy falsely,
priests rule at their direction,
and my people love it this way.
But what will you do when the end comes?”|Preserves complicity of people and uncertain priest-prophet relation.

6:1|Seek safety, people of Benjamin,
away from Jerusalem!
Blow the ram’s horn in Tekoa;
raise a signal over Beth-haccherem.
For disaster looms from the north,
great destruction.|Keeps flight from city rather than into it and all place names.
6:2|I will destroy Daughter Zion,\nbeautiful and pampered.|Chooses destroy sense of difficult verb; comparison alternative noted.
6:3|Shepherds with their flocks will come against her;\nthey will pitch tents all around her,\neach grazing his own patch.|Preserves invaders as pastoral encampment.

6:4|“Consecrate war against her!
Rise, let us attack at noon!
Alas for us, the day is declining;
evening shadows are lengthening.|Keeps holy-war preparation and attackers’ urgency.
6:5|Rise, let us attack at night\nand destroy her palaces!”|Retains shift to night attack.

6:6|For this is what the **LORD** of hosts says:
“Cut down trees and heap a siege ramp against Jerusalem.
This is the city to be called to account;
there is nothing but oppression within her.|Preserves divine order for siege and civic oppression charge.

6:7|As a well keeps its water flowing,
so she keeps her wickedness flowing.
Violence and devastation are heard in her;
sickness and wounds are constantly before me.|Keeps sustained evil-water image and physical injuries.

6:8|Accept correction, Jerusalem,
or I will turn away from you
and make you desolate,
a land without inhabitants.”|Preserves conditional warning and relational withdrawal.

6:9|This is what the **LORD** of hosts says:\n“They will thoroughly glean Israel’s remnant like a vine.\nPass your hand over the branches again, like a grape gatherer.”|Keeps repeated gleaning of remnant and difficult branch/basket term.

6:10|To whom can I speak and give warning
so they will listen?
Their ears are uncircumcised; they cannot pay attention.
The **LORD**’s word is an insult to them;
they take no pleasure in it.|Preserves circumcision image applied to hearing.

6:12|Their houses will pass to others,
together with fields and wives,
for I will stretch out my hand
